items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: he used to play, uh, spot jobs with Frankie Dues, with, with Edward Clem on the trombone.

ctx.x: Because it was in the church, yeah. Yeah. And who would play in there?

Well, different bands, you know, like, I played with Rene there, kid Rene played there. We played there many times there, St. Catharines Hall. I remember now. And, uh, I believe, uh, I don't know where Buddy played, uh, but I know they had different bands that used to play there. Whose Buddy? It's been so long, Buddy Petit, you know. Oh, yeah. They had so many different bands. At that time, they had Kid, uh, Howard, and they had, uh, uh, Chris Kelly. Chris Kelly's band. And they had, uh, the, uh, Pelican band…
Mm-hmm. What, that, St. Catherine Hall, did they have, uh, dances there every night or just on the weekend?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: And that Pelican band from uptown there, what you call them, playing trumpet there, Eddie, and they had a, what's the name, uh, it was Frankie Duesen. Frankie Duesen.

ctx.x: The Olivia band, I called it Olivier. Well, they had several other bands. Johnny Brown, here. Yeah, that's right. Well, that was Ragtime band. They called it Frank's band Ragtime band. Yeah. They joined in from Ragtime, to the Dixieland. Yeah.
And that Pelican band from uptown there, what you call them, playing trumpet there, Eddie, and they had a, what's the name, uh, it was Frankie Duesen. Frankie Duesen.

Oh, yeah. Well, that was the town, that was, uh, that was Ragtime band. Yeah. That was Ragtime band. They had the Frank's, ah, alright. I think that was a good one. That's when Frank takes the band, and he left John Pendleton, well, John Pendleton, you know, he could play a kind of style of music. No. Well, I had another fella. His name was Ned. Yeah. Yeah. That's Terry's band, but men like to travel around, so he went away. See, Frank's taken up on Edwark Clem.
